summary: This document changes the policy for adding entries to IANA's Secure Shell protocol parameter registries. Previously it was generally IETF Review, with a few needing Standards Action. It is now Expert Review. It updates RFCs 4250, 4716, 4819, and 8308.

eli5.summary: A club made it easier to add new items to its list. Now an expert says yes or no, rather than a big committee vote.

subtitle: SSH's IANA registries move from needing an RFC to needing a quick sign-off from designated experts.

tldr.problem: Adding a new value to most IANA Secure Shell (SSH) registries required IETF Review, which meant a full RFC process even for a small addition.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes the policy for the registries listed in its table from IETF Review to Expert Review, where designated experts judge each request after a three-week public review on a mailing list.
tldr.outcome: Registering new SSH algorithm names and similar values is lighter-weight. Only the Message Numbers and Publickey Subsystem Status Codes registries keep Standards Action.

facts.label: Unaffected registries
facts.value: Message Numbers and Publickey Subsystem Status Codes

today: RFC 9519 is a Proposed Standard and no RFC has obsoleted or updated it. It updates RFC 4250, RFC 4716, RFC 4819 and RFC 8308, which is where the affected registries were defined.

sections.title: Why the Policy Changed
sections.content:
The IANA Secure Shell (SSH) Protocol Parameters registry group was populated by several RFCs, including RFC 4250, RFC 4716, RFC 4819 and RFC 8308. Apart from some narrow value ranges that need Standards Action or are marked Private Use, new entries required IETF Review, as defined in RFC 8126.

This document changes that policy to Expert Review. The RFC says the change is in line with similar changes made for certain IPsec and TLS registries. The impetus was a February 2021 discussion on the CURDLE mailing list.
sections.eli5: Getting a new item on the SSH list used to be a long process. The rule was changed so it is faster, like the lists other groups already made easier.

sections.title: Which Registries Are Affected
sections.content:
Table 1 of the RFC lists the registries that move from IETF Review to Expert Review. They include the names registries for authentication methods, compression algorithms, encryption algorithms, key exchange methods, MAC algorithms and public key algorithms, plus connection protocol channel types, request names and subsystem names, service names, signal names, extension names and the publickey subsystem registries.

Some entries apply only to part of a registry. For three registries (channel connection failure reason codes, disconnection reason codes, and extended channel data transfer data_type_code), only the range 0x00000001-0xFDFFFFFF changes. For SSH public-key file header tags, header tags beginning with x- are excluded. Affected registries now list this document as a reference.

Two registries are not affected: Message Numbers and Publickey Subsystem Status Codes. They stay at Standards Action because their one-byte values are a limited resource.
sections.eli5: Almost every SSH list gets the easier rule. Two small lists with very few slots stay strict, because there are so few spaces to give out.

sections.title: How Expert Review Works
sections.content:
A registration request is sent to the ssh-reg-review@ietf.org mailing list. It is registered after a three-week review period, on the advice of one or more designated experts. Requests SHOULD use an appropriate subject, for example "Request to register value in SSH protocol parameters <specific parameter> registry".

Within the review period the experts approve or deny the request and tell the review list and IANA. A denial MUST include an explanation and, where applicable, suggestions for making the request succeed. To allow values to be allocated before publication, the experts may approve a registration once they are satisfied that a specification will be published.

A request that stays undetermined for longer than 21 days can be brought to the IESG's attention using the iesg@ietf.org mailing list.
sections.eli5: You post your idea where everyone can see it. After three weeks, the helpers say yes or no, and if it is no they must say why and how to fix it.

sections.title: The Experts and Their Criteria
sections.content:
The experts SHOULD check whether the proposed registration duplicates existing functionality (which is not permitted), whether it is likely to be of general applicability or useful only for a single application, and whether the registration description is clear.

IANA MUST only accept registry updates from the designated experts and the IESG, and SHOULD send requests from any other source to the review mailing list.

The RFC suggests appointing several experts who can represent the perspectives of different applications using SSH. If a decision could look like a conflict of interest for one expert, that expert SHOULD defer to the others.
sections.eli5: The helpers ask: is this the same as something we already have, will many people use it, and is it explained clearly? If a helper has a personal stake, they step back and let the others decide.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content: The IANA Considerations section says that the memo is entirely about updating the IANA Secure Shell (SSH) Protocol Parameters registry. The Security Considerations section is equally short: the memo does not change the Security Considerations of any of the updated RFCs.
sections.eli5: This change is only about the paperwork for adding things to a list. It does not change how safe SSH is.
